verdict.rationale: SumUp's first-party SDK docs describe an Offline Transactions feature that keeps card acceptance working when connectivity is unavailable or unreliable. It uses a store-and-forward flow: card data is cached securely on the device and uploaded later for authorization, which covers both halves of the story. Missing for 10: details on offline limits, risk/decline handling and which readers or SDKs support it; whether it is available in the standard merchant app beyond SDK integrations; independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a merchant-ops user, I can keep taking card payments when the internet drops, with transactions stored and forwarded when connectivity returns

citations.quote: In this store-and-forward flow, card data is captured and cached securely on the device, then uploaded later for processing and authorization.
Offline Transactions let merchants continue accepting card payments when internet connectivity is unavailable or unreliable.
